actual_nine_sentence_NV_spectral_rows.plain_English: In July 1964, inspecting rice ear by ear in a paddy at Anjiang Agricultural School in Hunan province, the instructor Yuan Longping spotted a peculiar plant.
The specimen launched a six-year hunt: Yuan and his colleagues could not breed a sterile line whose offspring reliably inherited the trait.
Yuan's assistant, Li Bihu, and Feng Keshan, a farm technician, found wild rice whose pollen was abortive.
Then came Yuan's decisive move: rather than withhold the strain, he distributed it to collaborators nationwide.
Hybrids need three distinct lines: a sterile line, one to maintain its sterility, and one to restore fertility in the hybrids.
Yan Longan's team in Jiangxi bred sterile lines and Zhang Xiancheng in Guangxi first identified a restorer line.
By 1976 hybrids were under cultivation on about 140,000 hectares.
The World Food Prize Foundation estimates that hybrid rice can yield up to a fifth more grain than conventional varieties.
Yet popular myth portrays him as a solitary genius.
